data.name: Aaban
data.gender_notes: Aaban is used as a male name in Persian naming tradition.
data.short_meaning: Waters; the angel of the waters; the eighth month of the Persian calendar
data.long_meaning: Aaban (آبان) is a Persian name meaning “Waters; the angel of the waters; the eighth month of the Persian calendar”. It comes from Persian Ābān (آبان), built on āb (آب) 'water'. Ābān is the eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar and the name of the yazata (angel) of the waters in Zoroastrian tradition. The name is therefore a calendrical and mythological name rather than a Qur'anic one.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aaban carries the meaning Waters; the angel of the waters. The Zoroastrian association with the yazata of waters is a religious tradition of pre-Islamic Iran, recorded here as tradition rather than as Islamic doctrine.
data.etymology: From Persian Ābān (آبان), built on āb (آب) 'water'. Used both as the eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar and as the name of the yazata of the waters.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaban total 10, reducing to 1. Number 1 is associated with leadership, independence and initiative. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What does the name Aaban mean?
faq.a: Aaban means Waters; the angel of the waters; the eighth month of the Persian calendar.

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Aaban?
What language does the name Aaban come from?
faq.a: Aaban is used in Persian and Urdu.

faq.q: Is Aaban a boy's name or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aaban is used as a male name.

faq.q: What is the eighth month of the Persian calendar called?
faq.a: The eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar is Ābān, which is also the name Aaban.

faq.q: How is Aaban written in Persian and Urdu?
faq.a: Aaban is written آبان in both Persian and Urdu, and आबान in Devanagari.

faq.q: What is the linguistic root of Aaban?
faq.a: The root of Aaban is Persian Ābān (آبان), from āb (آب) water.

faq.q: What is the etymology of Aaban?
faq.a: From Persian Ābān (آبان), built on āb (آب) water. It is both the eighth month of the Iranian solar calendar and the name of the yazata of the waters.

faq.q: Does Aaban appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aaban is of Persian origin and is not a Qur'anic name.

Ābān is the name of the yazata (angel) of the waters in Zoroastrian tradition and the eighth month of the Iranian calendar. That is a pre-Islamic Iranian religious association; the name is also used by Muslim families as a Persian heritage name.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aaban verified?
faq.a: Yes. The meaning rests on the Persian month-name and the Zoroastrian yazata of the waters, both built on āb, water.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Aaban?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaban total 10, reducing to 1. Number 1 is traditionally associated with leadership, independence and initiative. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Aaban?
faq.a: Variants and alternative transliterations include Aban and Aabaan.

faq.q: Where is the name Aaban used today?
faq.a: Aaban circulates chiefly in Persian and Urdu naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
